vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2253: Dashboard recovery guardian — make the supervisor sidecar durable via a systemd user unit

plan.title: Dashboard recovery guardian — durable supervisor via systemd user unit
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: The dashboard's recovery guardian (the supervisor sidecar at src/supervisor/server.ts, port 3012) is started as a detached child by `pan up` — nothing supervises the supervisor itself, so if it crashes or is killed the dashboard is unguarded and can go dark as in the 2026-07-02 incident. Separately, the watchdog's health probe (src/supervisor/watchdog.ts:204) trusts any 200 on /api/health, so a squatter grabbing port 3011 counts as healthy.
narratives.Proposal: Wrap the existing supervisor sidecar in a systemd user unit (overdeck-supervisor.service) with Restart=on-failure + StartLimitBurst so the guardian survives its own death and crash-loops back off. Route `pan up`/`pan down`/`pan restart --dashboard` through the unit (with a full fallback to today's detached spawn when systemctl --user is unavailable). `systemctl --user stop` becomes the operator-intent latch. Add identity verification (repoRoot + mode==='primary') to the watchdog probe, and surface a loud operator notification when the unit gives up, reusing the existing restart-announcer pipeline.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Full-stack cold-boot recovery after a machine reboot (unit is NOT enabled at boot; lingering NOT enabled) — follow-up issue.
- Duplicating the #2286 fix for the 15s restart health-timeout — that is a prerequisite owned elsewhere.
- Making systemd own the dashboard process directly — rejected to avoid PAN-1714 dual-ownership churn.
- Non-Linux service managers (launchd, Windows services) — those use the existing detached-spawn fallback.
- Changing the watchdog's existing dead-vs-busy thresholds, give-up counters, or deacon-patrol logic.

autoDecisions.summary: Unit supervises the supervisor sidecar (overdeck-supervisor.service), not the dashboard process directly.
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids PAN-1714 dual-ownership churn; additive (dashboard launch untouched); closes the 'guardian has no guardian' gap minimally. Deviates from the issue's suggested overdeck-dashboard.service name to reflect what it guards.

autoDecisions.summary: Cold-boot / full-stack reboot recovery is out of scope; unit not enabled at boot, lingering off.
autoDecisions.rationale: The unit must not start into a stackless post-reboot environment; full-stack boot bring-up is a larger separate change.

autoDecisions.summary: #2286 treated as a prerequisite and not duplicated.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue explicitly declares #2286 a prerequisite; the dashboard-restart-under-load path is fixed there.

autoDecisions.summary: Give-up notification reuses the existing restart-announcer instead of a new CLI verb.
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids skills<->CLI lockstep lint churn; the announcer already renders the gaveUp restart-status.

autoDecisions.summary: Identity verification reuses the already-shipped getDashboardIdentity() {repoRoot, mode} contract (#2252).
autoDecisions.rationale: No new health field needed; mirror waitForDashboardHealthPromise's expectedIdentity logic.

items.title: Add systemdUserAvailable() capability detector

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/systemd.ts exporting an async `systemdUserAvailable(): Promise<boolean>` that returns true only when a per-user systemd manager is usable (e.g. `systemctl --user is-system-running` / `--version` succeeds via execAsync AND a user DBus session exists). It MUST return false — never throw — in containers, CI, macOS, and non-systemd Linux. Use execAsync/spawn only (never execSync). This is the single gate all routing beads consult; export a stable async signature.

items.title: Given a host with a working `systemctl --user`, systemdUserAvailable() resolves to true
Given `systemctl` missing or `--user` unusable (no DBus session), the function resolves to false and does not throw
The detector uses execAsync/spawn only — grep of src/lib/systemd.ts returns no execSync usage
Generate + install/uninstall the overdeck-supervisor.service user unit with control helpers

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Serialized after systemd-detect via a blocks edge (both author src/lib/systemd.ts); no other item edits this file, so it is conflict-free once detect lands.
expected_outputs: unit-render snapshot + install idempotency tests pass

narrative.Action: In src/lib/systemd.ts add: (a) a pure renderer that produces the `overdeck-supervisor.service` unit text with `[Service] Type=simple`, `ExecStart=<abs Node22 binary> <abs dist/supervisor/server.js>` (reuse resolveSupervisorBundle() from src/lib/supervisor.ts and process.execPath), `Environment=OVERDECK_SUPERVISOR_PORT=<port>` and any env the sidecar needs, `Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=5`, `StartLimitIntervalSec` and `StartLimitBurst` (bounded crash-loop), and `[Install] WantedBy=` DELIBERATELY OMITTED (NonGoal: no boot start); (b) an idempotent installer that writes ~/.config/systemd/user/overdeck-supervisor.service only when content differs and runs `systemctl --user daemon-reload`; (c) control helpers `startSupervisorUnit()`, `stopSupervisorUnit()`, `isSupervisorUnitActive()`, `isSupervisorUnitFailed()`, `uninstallSupervisorUnit()` — all async via execAsync/spawn. Export a shared UNIT_NAME constant.

items.title: The renderer produces a unit whose ExecStart is an absolute Node 22 path + absolute dist/supervisor/server.js path, with Restart=on-failure, StartLimitIntervalSec, and StartLimitBurst present (verified by a snapshot test)
The rendered unit contains no `[Install]`/`WantedBy=` section (no boot enablement) — asserted by the snapshot test
install is idempotent: given an already-identical unit file, the installer writes nothing and does not error (re-running preserves the file mtime/content)
isSupervisorUnitFailed() returns true when `systemctl --user is-failed` reports failed and returns false (never throws) when the unit is absent
`pan up` starts the supervisor through the systemd unit when available, else detached fallback

narrative.Action: At the supervisor-start block in `pan up` (src/cli/index.ts:959-969), when systemdUserAvailable() is true: install the unit (idempotent) then `startSupervisorUnit()` (a no-op when already active per NFR-3), logging the systemd-managed path. When false: fall back to today's startSupervisorProcessSync() unchanged. Never surface an error on the fallback path. Do NOT restart a healthy supervisor on re-run.

items.title: Given systemdUserAvailable() true, `pan up` installs the unit and calls startSupervisorUnit(); the detached startSupervisorProcessSync() is NOT called
Given systemdUserAvailable() false, `pan up` falls back to startSupervisorProcessSync() and surfaces no error
Given an already-active unit, a second `pan up` does not restart or duplicate the supervisor (idempotent — startSupervisorUnit resolves without a restart call)
`pan down` stops the supervisor via `systemctl --user stop` (operator-intent latch)

narrative.Action: At the supervisor-stop block in `pan down` (src/cli/index.ts:1178-1185), when the unit is installed/active call `stopSupervisorUnit()` (`systemctl --user stop`) — a clean stop systemd will NOT auto-restart — instead of the direct-SIGTERM stopSupervisorProcessSync(). Fall back to stopSupervisorProcessSync() when systemctl --user is unavailable. This makes `systemctl --user stop` (or `pan down`) the durable stay-down latch.

items.title: Given the unit is active, `pan down` calls stopSupervisorUnit() (systemctl --user stop), NOT a direct PID SIGTERM
After stopSupervisorUnit(), isSupervisorUnitActive() returns false and `pan down` issues no restart command (the stopped unit survives as inactive)
Given systemctl --user unavailable, `pan down` falls back to stopSupervisorProcessSync() and stops the detached supervisor
`pan restart --dashboard` skips the manual supervisor cycle when the unit owns the supervisor

narrative.Action: In restartCommand's dashboard case (src/cli/commands/restart.ts:214-219), gate the manual stopSupervisorProcessSync()/startSupervisorProcessSync() cycle behind `!(systemdUserAvailable() && isSupervisorUnitActive())`. When the unit owns the supervisor, do not kill/respawn it — systemd keeps it alive across the dashboard restart, avoiding the dual-ownership fight (hazard H1). Preserve existing behavior (OVERDECK_SKIP_SUPERVISOR_CYCLE guard, non-fatal catch) otherwise.

items.title: Given the unit is active, `pan restart --dashboard` does NOT call stopSupervisorProcessSync()/startSupervisorProcessSync()
Given the unit is not active (detached mode), `pan restart --dashboard` preserves the existing stop+start supervisor cycle
SupervisorWatchdog health probe verifies dashboard identity (repoRoot + mode)

narrative.Action: In SupervisorWatchdog.runCheck() (src/supervisor/watchdog.ts:211-217), after `response.ok`, parse the /api/health body and treat the probe as a HARD failure (like a non-OK response) when the identity does not match the host primary: repoRoot !== the expected host root OR mode !== 'primary'. Mirror waitForDashboardHealthPromise's expectedIdentity check (platform-lifecycle.ts:219-227). Add the expected repoRoot to SupervisorWatchdogConfig (default process.cwd() at supervisor launch) so a squatter answering 200 is classified unhealthy. Keep timeouts classified as busy, not identity failures.

items.title: Given /api/health returns 200 with mode!=='primary' (e.g. a peer/squatter), runCheck() classifies it as a hard failure and increments consecutiveHardFailures
Given /api/health returns 200 with a foreign repoRoot, runCheck() classifies it unhealthy (does not count as healthy)
Given /api/health returns 200 with matching repoRoot and mode==='primary', runCheck() marks the dashboard healthy and resets failure counters
Surface an operator notification when the supervisor unit gives up (failed state)

narrative.Action: Add a dashboard-side check (async, execAsync/spawn only — NFR-1) that calls isSupervisorUnitFailed(); when true and not already announced, write a give-up restart-status (trigger 'watchdog'/'supervisor', gaveUp:true, error naming the unit) so the existing restart-announcer (describeRestart -> 'Supervisor watchdog GAVE UP ... manual intervention required') surfaces it in the activity feed at level 'error'. Dedupe using the existing restart-announcer last-announced-ts mechanism so it announces once per failure episode. Skip entirely when systemctl --user is unavailable.

items.title: Given isSupervisorUnitFailed() true, an error-level activity entry stating the supervisor gave up / manual intervention required is emitted exactly once per failure episode
Given the unit is active (not failed), no give-up notification is emitted
The unit-failure check uses execAsync/spawn only — grep of the changed file shows no execSync
Document the durable-guardian model, operator commands, and fallback

expected_outputs: the doc references overdeck-supervisor.service and the systemctl --user operator commands

narrative.Action: Add a 'Dashboard recovery guardian' section to docs/OVERDECK_DEV_SOP.md documenting: the two-tier model (systemd unit keeps the supervisor alive; the supervisor keeps the dashboard alive); operator commands (`systemctl --user status/stop/start overdeck-supervisor.service`, and that `pan down` = stay-down latch); the non-systemd fallback; and the NonGoal (no cold-boot recovery). Note #2286 as the restart-under-load prerequisite.
